svg.title: iOS · Projects · portrait
svg.desc: Mirrors App/ProjectsView.swift (header, ProjectCard) + App/CaptureFilterBar.swift (CaptureFilterBar) + App/SceneSearch.swift (SceneSearchField, SceneTagChips, SceneTagLine): manual large title, scene search field, the shared segmented capture filter (All · Photos · Interval · Video) and the subject-tag chip row share one list row — 15pt above the title, 10pt above the 34pt search capsule, 8pt above and below the filter bar, chips flush after it with 8pt below, first card at 238. **2026-09-06** the title row gained the SHARING PILL opposite it (see below) and the search row gave up its trailing 129pt to SORT: a Capture · Added · Edit · Size menu and a direction triangle, applied after the search, the kind filter and the tag chips — narrowest question last. Capture is the shoot's own date; **Added** (2026-09-07) is `CaptureProject.addedAt`, when the project arrived in THIS library — the two are only the same question on a device that shoots everything it holds, because every import path deliberately keeps the shoot's own date, so a timelapse shot last August lands under last August however recently it turned up, and this is the axis that finds it again; it is stamped at registration, re-stamped by hand on the two paths that copy an existing record (an archive import, a DNG-archive clone) so they don't inherit the source device's answer, and backfilled once for an existing library from each project folder's own creation date — the filesystem has been recording this all along. Edit is `CaptureProject.modifiedAt`, stamped only where a PERSON changes a project (rename, grade, rotate, nominate a frame, add or delete a blend or an encoding) and never by a background metadata probe, falling back to the newest blended clip's date and then to the capture date for a library that predates the field; Size is a stored measurement (`sizeBytes`/`sizeMeasuredAt`) re-taken only for projects edited since it was made, so the first size sort walks the library once and later ones walk only what changed — a mini spinner rides the menu label while it does, and a project not yet measured holds the unknown end of the list rather than posing as an empty one. Both the axis and the direction are remembered between launches. Search matches a project's name, its subject tags (raw and labelled) and the free-form elements the on-device analysis named; chips narrow to projects carrying EVERY selected tag. Both are hidden while the library is empty, and the chip row is drawn only from tags that actually exist in the library. One card per original. **2026-09-06 the blended-clip strip is gone**: the card carried a horizontal scroller of clip thumbnails under the text column, and it cost every blended project ~78pt of list for a jump the project's own screen already offers — Steven's call after living with it. Its removal also takes a macOS bug with it, and by removing the cause rather than working around it: an inner NSScrollView swallows the vertical wheel and trackpad events a nested horizontal scroller has no use for instead of passing them up the responder chain, so the Projects list stuck whenever the pointer crossed a strip. AppKit exposes no switch for that (the fix would have been an NSScrollView subclass forwarding vertical-dominant events to its nextResponder); with no nesting there is nothing to forward. The count line — "2 blended clips · 1.4 GB", accent when there are any — still says they exist. Every card's size line ends with a SOURCE-FORMAT pill (SourceFormatPill): an icon for what the source assets are (stills / footage), the file type they were written in (DNG · JPG · MOV), and FLAT when the shoot was captured flat — read from the run's own sidecar (stills: `capture_log.json`; video: `sequence.json`, where either the Capture Flat request or the Apple Log that actually engaged counts). The pill is 18pt tall against the size line's 14.3, so it costs 4pt to any card whose text column already outgrows its 64pt thumbnail (cards 1 and 2 here) and nothing at all to the ones the thumbnail still sets (card 3). A VIDEO project's card carries a second 12pt secondary line under its format line — the shoot's source composition: "N source clips" (imports read "1 source clip"), and, when the sequence sidecar records burst segments above the base rate, "· N bursts at R fps" (one burst: "1 burst at…"; mixed burst rates collapse to a range, "120–240 fps"). The line is video-kind only and costs those cards 16pt: interval cards already carry their count in the format line ("Interval · N photos" — bursts can't exist there), and Photo-mode cards stay ONE asset (no counts; their burst frames are stacking material, owned by project detail). An analysed project carries a tag line under its size line (up to 3 chips, then "+N") — without it the chips would filter by something invisible; an unanalysed project's card keeps its original height. A project tagged by the silent Apple Vision pass at capture time ends that same tag line with a 10pt sparkles glyph (accent at 70%, 6pt gap) — it marks "the app guessed this" rather than "you agreed to this", and disappears once an Auto rename & tag proposal is applied; being inside the tag line, it adds no height. Swipe-to-delete on cards; context menu for preview/new blended clip/details/delete. Card rows hang their 14pt rhythm below them (listRowInsets top 0 / bottom 14). **2026-09-14 (data model M2, code first — desc only, nothing drawn changes):** the rows, their order, the filter counts and the chip row come from the library's SQLite index (`AppModel.projectIDs(for:)` over one `ProjectListQuery`), and the search field is the index's full-text search: every typed word matches by PREFIX ("brid" finds bridge; "idge" no longer does — by decision) against the project's name or original file name, its tags AND their chip labels ("weather" finds Sky & weather), the model's elements, and — new — its assets' titles, captions, keywords, creator, place and camera; every word must land on the same project, so typing more narrows. A word with no letter or digit ("&") is not a term. The dated fallback title of an unnamed project ("Photo 13. 9. at 13:49") is a rendering, not a field, so a typed date fragment no longer finds it; "photo" now also finds unnamed interval shoots through their original name ("1057 photos"). Sort ties are the same as before (the capture date, then the id, turning with the sort). Verified 2026-09-14: 36 launch-hook cases (`LL_FILTER`, `LL_QUERY`, `LL_CHIPS`, `LL_DUMP_ORDER`) identical before and after on the Mac and the iPhone 16 Pro simulator bar the three search cases above.
svg.text: mirrors App/ProjectsView.swift — header (title + SceneSearchField + CaptureFilterBar + SceneTagChips) · ProjectCard incl. source/burst line + SourceFormatPill + SceneTagLine · no blended-clip strip since 2026-09-06
